head: 53c6156e9aa5bb1a0291bb2ac2a6b23bb8c7bdfd
summary:
The build matches the design. Every departure from it was declared, and every check I re-ran passes:
- The acceptance script exits 0.
- The filtered rule tests pass 157/157.
- rules-parity reads AGREE, unchanged.
- The harness reads CLEAN with 16/16 plants AS-RECORDED, including F51, S55, S56 and S57, the texts never put through Fitness before.
- RuleCases C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 are green.

I recomputed the before-fix set on my own from the 1105c3f patterns. It is exactly the 42 ids in closed_by. Every id named in census, aliases and outside_the_bound exists with the verdict it states, and every row has the verdict the widened patterns give it.

Two ordinary save-and-restore spellings get past rule C. In both, the corpus's own bounded_by.member says the spelling is a member, yet the census omits it:
- **Registry-provider cmdlets.** Rename-Item or Move-Item of Explorer\Advanced, and `Rename-ItemProperty -Name HiddenOld -NewName Hidden`, the restore that pairs with W64. This family is the one O-017 claimed closed.
- **reg.exe.** `reg copy` into Explorer\Advanced.

Each gets 0 hits from all 9 window patterns (my probe used .NET Regex, read straight from .taad/fitness.yaml). Two smaller shapes are filed as extras:
- reg.exe called through Start-Process -ArgumentList or an argument array, the way this repo launches programs;
- a named `name:` argument on DeleteValue or SetValue in src.

The defect is latent: no registry write exists in src/ or tests/window/.

Second round: Second lap, read adversarially. I went back over every reader and pattern this diff adds:
- **The acceptance script's yaml and Fact readers.** Both throw when an entry or Fact is missing; neither silently reads the wrong block.
- **The widened src and rule-C patterns, against what their input formats allow.** Lone CR, CRLF and U+2028 are all treated the same by .NET ReadAllLines and by Python's universal-newline read with `[^\r\n]`. A BOM before `\breg` or the New-Item lookbehind still leaves a word boundary. Every new branch uses `[ \t]` only. Single-quoted YAML with doubled quotes reads the same in SettledPatterns and in PyYAML: the harness S57 row is AS-RECORDED.
- **The closed_by repeat recipe.** I had already re-derived it.

One new member of the provider-cmdlet family that O-017 declared closed gets past rule C. Microsoft's documented registry idiom passes the parent key as -Path and the leaf as -Name: `New-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer' -Name 'Advanced' -Force`. That line recreates Explorer\Advanced empty, the same operation as fire row W60, and gets 0 hits from all 9 window patterns, because :1124 needs `Explorer\Advanced` adjacent on the line. It is not the m4 waiver's split path: m4 covers a parent open followed by a separate child call. No line in tests/window today has `-Name Advanced`, so the fix adds no stray hit. Nothing else new.

findings.claim:
Rule C lets through three registry-provider moves that change Explorer\Advanced's values. O-017 claimed this family closed, and the corpus's own bounded_by.member names moving or renaming the key as members:
- `Rename-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -NewName AdvancedBackup`;
- `Move-Item -Path 'HKCU:\...\Explorer\Advanced' -Destination 'HKCU:\Software\FsaBackup'`;
- `Rename-ItemProperty -Path $adv -Name HiddenOld -NewName Hidden`, the restore half of W64's save.

I fed each line alone to the 9 window patterns read from .taad/fitness.yaml, and each got 0 hits:
- :1124 knows only Remove-Item, New-Item and Clear-Item beside the ItemProperty verbs.
- :1125 looks for Hidden only after `-Name`, and `HiddenOld` fails its `\b`.

Renaming or moving the key leaves Hidden absent at its path, which is the same effect as W49 (Remove-Item, a fire row) and the measured delete (showAll 1 to 0). The -NewName restore writes Hidden. The census entry 'New-Item, Clear-Item, Remove-Item on the key' names neither cmdlet as fire, miss or out, so the census is incomplete for a family the build declared closed.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1124-1125 (rule C); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json:5 (bounded_by.member) and :134 (census, registry-provider cmdlets); W64 at :295. Probe: a pwsh script that reads the entry as SettledPatterns does; each of the three lines gave hits=[].

quote.text: sets, deletes, imports, copies, moves, renames or recreates its Hidden or ShowSuperHidden value or the key itself

findings.fix:
Widen in place, so the count stays 9:
1. In :1124, extend the lookaround group to `(Remove-Item|New-Item|Clear-Item|Rename-Item|Move-Item)`.
2. In :1125, change `-Name[ \t]+` to `-(New)?Name[ \t]+`.

Add these fire rows, all before=quiet:
- W74: `Rename-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -NewName AdvancedBackup`
- W75: `Move-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -Destination 'HKCU:\Software\FsaBackup'`
- W76: `Rename-ItemProperty -Path $adv -Name HiddenOld -NewName Hidden`

Add W74-W76 to closed_by and to the census and aliases under the registry-provider cmdlets.
findings.class_of: registry-provider cmdlets that change Explorer\Advanced's values

findings.claim:
`reg copy HKCU\Software\FsaBackup "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced" /s /f` gets 0 hits from rule C. It is the restore half of a reg.exe save/restore, it writes Hidden back into the key, and it works unelevated on HKCU.

The :1126 reg pattern knows only add, delete and import. The corpus's census for the reg.exe type lists the same three verbs as if that were every write verb, while bounded_by.member names 'copies' as a member.

The other reg.exe write verbs, restore and load, need SeRestorePrivilege/admin, so `copy` is the one an unelevated window script can reach.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1126; ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json census 'reg.exe' (:140-146). Probe: `reg copy ... Explorer\Advanced /s /f` gave hits=[]; `& reg.exe copy $backup $adv /s /f` gave hits=[].
findings.fix:
1. In :1126, change `(add\b[^\r\n]*(` to `((add|copy)\b[^\r\n]*(`. The count stays 9.
2. Add fire row W77, `reg copy HKCU\Software\FsaBackup "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced" /s /f` (before=quiet). Add it to closed_by, and add a `copy into the key` member to the reg.exe census.
3. Pin `& reg.exe copy $backup $adv /s /f` as a miss row (path in a variable).

findings.claim:
When reg.exe is called through an argument array, rule C's :1126 pattern sees nothing. It needs whitespace and then the verb right after `reg`/`reg.exe`. Two lines that get 0 hits:
- `Start-Process reg.exe -ArgumentList 'import', $file -Wait`
- `& reg @('add', $adv, '/v', 'Hidden', '/t', 'REG_DWORD', '/d', '1', '/f')`

This repo launches programs exactly that way: WindowCases.ps1:473 uses Start-Process -ArgumentList, and :685 and :5743 use ArgumentList.Add. CC-007 asks for array-form arguments to be tested. Neither shape is fire or a pinned miss in the corpus, so a later change to it would go unseen.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1126; tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:473, :685, :5743; probe hits=[] for both lines.
findings.fix: Pin both lines as miss rows (window, before=quiet). Name 'reg.exe through an argument array or Start-Process' under bounded_by.outside_the_bound, beside the alias gap.
findings.class_of: native reg.exe invoked through an argument array

findings.claim:
The src value-name patterns need the quote to follow `(` directly, so the named-argument spelling gets 0 hits from the src Fact's 6 patterns. Examples: `key.DeleteValue(name: "Hidden");` and `key.SetValue(name: "Hidden", value: 1)`.

The corpus fires the named-argument spelling of the open (B08 `writable: true`, B37 `rights: RegistryRights.SetValue`) but neither fires nor pins it for the value name, so the bound is inconsistent and unrecorded.
findings.fix: Either widen the src pattern in both copies to `\([ \t]*(name[ \t]*:[ \t]*)?@?"` and add fire rows, or pin `key.DeleteValue(name: "Hidden");` as a src miss row.
findings.class_of: named-argument spellings of a value-name write

findings.claim:
`New-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer' -Name 'Advanced' -Force | Out-Null` passes rule C with 0 hits from all 9 patterns. So do the unquoted `-Name Advanced` and positional-path forms (probe: .NET Regex on the patterns read from .taad/fitness.yaml).

Passing the parent as -Path and the new key's leaf as -Name is the registry provider's documented New-Item spelling. The line does to Explorer\Advanced exactly what fire row W60 does: -Force recreates the existing key empty (PowerShell/PowerShell#5444), which deletes Hidden.

:1124 fires New-Item only when `Explorer\{1,2}Advanced` stands adjacent on the line, so the cmdlet M1 added is caught in one of its two ordinary spellings. O-017 answered this family as closed. The corpus census entry 'New-Item, Clear-Item, Remove-Item on the key' lists only W49, W60 and W61. Nothing pins the -Name form, so a later change to it would go unseen. This is not the waived m4 split path, which is a parent open followed by a separate child call; here it is one cmdlet call with its own -Path/-Name pair.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1124. ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json W60 (:291) and census (:134). Probe: hits=[] for three spellings of `New-Item ... Explorer' -Name Advanced -Force`; hits=[0] for W60's adjacent-path form. Grep: no `-Name Advanced` anywhere under tests/window today.
findings.fix:
1. Add a top-level alternative inside the existing :1124 pattern, so the count stays 9: `...[^\r\n]*Explorer\\{1,2}Advanced|(?<![\w$-])New-Item(?![\w-])[^\r\n]*-Name[ \t]+[''"]?Advanced\b`. This catches both parameter orders.
2. Add fire row W78: `New-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer' -Name 'Advanced' -Force | Out-Null` (window, before=quiet).
3. Add W78 to closed_by and to the census and aliases entry 'New-Item, Clear-Item, Remove-Item on the key'.
findings.class_of: registry-provider cmdlets that change Explorer\Advanced's values

obligations.evidence: I ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-103-ExplorerAdvancedRightsOpen.Tests.ps1`: 'All checks held.', exit 0. It reads both src copies and rule C from the files.

Corpus rows B30, B31, B33-B37 and B40 (ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json:209-219) are fire. The marker `RegistryRights\]?(\.|::)(SetValue|WriteKey|FullControl)` is at fitness.yaml:286 and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:291. The Theory passes.
B32, B38 and B41 are quiet rows and pass. My probe also has a ReadKey open of the key quiet in src.
B42-B50 are fire rows and B51 is a quiet row; the src :285, :287 and :289 widenings fire on them.
B27, B28, B29 and B39 are miss rows (corpus:206-208, :218) and pass.
W35 and W41-W43 are fire rows under the new :1130 pattern; the acceptance script prints ok for them.
W36, W37, W38 and W46 fire through the quoted-only branch of :1130; harness plant S51 (W37) reads AS-RECORDED quiet/fire.
W39 and W40 fire; so do W65-W67 (flags strings), and my probe also fires on `'QueryValues,SetValue'` with no space.
W29, W44, W47, W68 and W73 are quiet and W55 fires. In my probe an empty string `''` stays quiet, which is right, because it binds as $false.
W48, W49, W50 and W57 are fire rows; plant S53 reads AS-RECORDED.
W09, W10, W11, W51, W52 and W58 fire; plants S54 and S55 read AS-RECORDED in my harness run.
W45, W53, W54, W56 and W59 are miss rows. W60 became a fire row per accepted M1.

No old row changed its verdict: my recompute against 1105c3f flagged no row that was caught then and is not fire now. TheCorpusHolds... asserts 9 window and 6 src patterns (ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.cs:86-87). Parity is unchanged.

closed_by (corpus:172-178) lists 42 ids and pre_fix_commit 1105c3f. I recomputed against `git show 1105c3f:.taad/fitness.yaml`: the now=fire rows that the old patterns let through are exactly those 42, with no difference either way.

I ran all of these:
- rules-parity: AGREE 18/22/48/69.
- The harness over 16 rows: clean baseline CLEAN, 16 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0.
- RuleCases C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005: all held.
- The filtered tests: 157/157.
Plants F51 (RegDelete prefix), S53, S54 and S55 (/v branch) read AS-RECORDED in my own harness run. Rows B49 and W56-W60 pass the Theory and match my independent .NET probe.

Every fix the critic listed is in: the ItemProperty verbs widened at :1124/:1125, New-Item|Clear-Item in the lookaround, W60-W64 and plant S56. But it was answered as 'closed as the class registry-provider cmdlets that change Explorer\Advanced's values', and Rename-Item and Move-Item of the key, and `Rename-ItemProperty -NewName Hidden`, still pass rule C. The corpus's bounded_by.member names those moves as members, and the census does not list them (finding m1).

The quoted-name alternative at :1130 is widened to `['"][^'"\r\n]*\b(SetValue|WriteKey|FullControl)\b[^'"\r\n]*['"]`. W65-W67 fire and W68/W73 stay quiet; S57 reads AS-RECORDED. No other write-capable rights spelling I probed got through.
:1124 holds only full cmdlet names. W69 and W70 are miss rows. bounded_by.aliases_are_a_known_gap and the rule-C `because` say aliases are a known gap.
The _note at corpus:2 is rewritten ('it is not the code before SL-103'), and the closed_by key names the ids, 1105c3f and how_to_repeat. Checked against my recompute.
Waived to SC-308; bounded_by.not_pinned records it. My own check found census and aliases consistent with the rows today.
Waived to SC-309; bounded_by.not_pinned names rights in a variable, the using alias and the split path.
Waived to SC-310; bounded_by.not_pinned names the missing multi-line plant.

cases.evidence: ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json B30, B31, B33-B37 and B40 carry each qualification (short, fully qualified, | combined, ReadSubTree and Default checks, named rights:, OpenBaseKey, two-backslash non-verbatim path). The Theory feeds each line to the Fact's patterns.
B32 (ReadKey), B38 (CreateSubKey) and B41 (QueryValues) are quiet rows fed to the src patterns.

B42 and B43 (DeleteValue, with and without false), B44 and B50 (DeleteSubKeyTree, DeleteSubKey), B45-B47 and B49 (declared RegDeleteValue, RegDeleteKeyValue, SHDeleteValue, RegDeleteTree) and B48 (called RegDeleteKeyValueW).
B39 (FromHandle with a constant), B27, B28 and B29 are miss rows asserted quiet.
W35 (::SetValue), W41 (-bor), W42 (Default with FullControl) and W43 (the C# line in the hook) are fed to rule C's patterns read from the yaml.
W36, W37, W38 and W46 are quoted strings alone as the second argument.
W39 ([Security.AccessControl.RegistryRights]'SetValue') and W40 (all-string OpenBaseKey with 'FullControl'), plus W65-W67.
W29 (one argument), W44 (enum ReadKey) and W47 ($false) are quiet; W55 ('True') fires.
W48 (DeleteValue('Hidden')), W49 (Remove-Item of the key), W50 (::DeleteSubKeyTree) and W57 (RegDeleteKeyValueW).
W51 and W52 (reg import), W58 (reg add $adv /v Hidden), and W09, W10 and W11 still fire. Plants S54 and S55 put the import and /v texts through Fitness.
W45, W53, W54, W56 and W59 are miss rows. W60 is now fire per accepted M1 (declared).
The 63 old rows are in the Theory with their `before` checked against the frozen SrcBefore/WindowBefore; TheCorpusHolds... asserts 9/6.

No standing test runs the old patterns, apart from the acceptance script for the rights-open subset. The run is recorded in closed_by.how_to_repeat. I re-derived it from the 1105c3f yaml: exactly the 42 closed_by ids fail.
I re-ran rules-parity (AGREE, unchanged), the harness (CLEAN, 16/16 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits) and RuleCases C-001/C-003/C-004/C-005 (all held).

drift:
Nothing departed from the design without being declared:
- W60 moved from miss to fire, with W61-W67 and plants S56/S57 added, per accepted M1/M2.
- The bare aliases were dropped per m1.
- closed_by was added per m2.
- Doc comments in ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.cs were reworded.
- CreateSubKey was dropped from the marker.
The build declared each of these.

docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still describes both guards as 'closed as a class'. The corpus and both `because` texts now say 'bounded by producer'. This is declared as a follow-up but not done.
Nothing new departed from the design without being declared. Round 1's drift notes stand.
